articles.title: Rochdale Town Hall to host Ignite Fire Festival from November 20 to 22
articles.excerpt: The Ignite Fire Festival returns to Rochdale Town Hall and gardens, featuring a light and fire trail, live performances, and festive activities.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Town Hall and its gardens will be the venue for the Ignite Fire Festival from November 20 to 22, 2026. This popular event, which is free to attend, is expected to attract around 10,000 visitors, building on its success from previous years.

The festival will feature a light and fire trail with six walk-through zones themed around the human body. Attendees will experience an immersive installation created by Walk The Plank, which has previously been showcased in Ireland and Canada.

The event will run nightly from 5pm to 8pm.

In addition to the fire trail, the festival will include a Fire Garden with illuminated sculptures, performances by the Drum Machine collective, and fire shows from local groups like Skylight Circus Arts and Travelling Light Circus.

Food and seasonal drinks will also be available for purchase, including flame-cooked hot food and mulled wine.

On the final evening, November 22, a special festive lights switch-on will take place, featuring Father Christmas and the Mayor of Rochdale. Councillor Sue Smith highlighted the festival's role in celebrating the borough and attracting visitors from across Greater Manchester.

articles.title: Lachlan Lanskey joins Rochdale Hornets on one-year deal for 2027 season
articles.excerpt: Australia-born Ireland international Lachlan Lanskey has signed with Rochdale Hornets for the upcoming season after leaving Keighley Cougars.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Hornets have confirmed the signing of Lachlan Lanskey on a one-year deal for the 2027 season. The Australia-born Ireland international joins the club following his departure from Keighley Cougars, where he played for three years.

Lanskey, a back-rower, is a product of the Brisbane Broncos’ youth system and has represented Queensland at various youth levels.

Although he did not make an NRL appearance, he played for Brisbane Tigers in the Queensland Cup before moving to the UK in 2023 to join Whitehaven.

Currently, Lanskey represents Ireland internationally, having made his debut last autumn in a Test Series against Wales. He recently starred in a match against Scotland in the Celtic Cup, marking his third cap for the Wolfhounds.

Expressing his excitement about the move, Lanskey stated, “I’m really happy to be getting on board for the 2027 season.” His addition is expected to bolster Rochdale's squad as they prepare for the upcoming Championship campaign.

articles.title: Scrooge screening with live orchestra comes to Heywood Civic
articles.excerpt: The 1951 film starring Alastair Sim will be shown with a live score from the three-piece FB Pocket Orchestra on Saturday 14 November.
articles.content_html:
A screening of the classic film Scrooge with a live three-piece orchestra is coming to Heywood Civic on Saturday 14 November.

The event starts at 8pm and pairs the 1951 film starring Alastair Sim with music performed by the FB Pocket Orchestra. The production is touring in the film’s 75th anniversary year.

The venue lists a running time of 90 minutes. Its Pay What You Can prices are £8.40 at the lower rate, £10.50 standard and £12.60 at the higher rate, all including the booking fee.

Rather than a stage adaptation, this is a showing of the film with live musical accompaniment. It follows Ebenezer Scrooge’s encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Future in the familiar Charles Dickens story.

The organisers say the music is based on Richard Addinsell’s original score. Heywood Civic’s listing explains that Paul Stevenson reconstructed the score by listening to and transcribing the film soundtrack, creating an arrangement for the ensemble.

The film has a U certificate. For local families and cinema fans, the event offers a chance to hear live musicians accompany a black-and-white Christmas classic at a borough venue.

Heywood Civic is on LCpl Stephen Shaw MC Way, Heywood, OL10 1LW. Tickets and the venue’s pricing information are available at https://heywoodcivic.co.uk/event/scrooge-u-live-to-film/. Check availability and the venue’s accessibility information before booking.

The event was announced in a press release supplied by FB Music and Media, with the date, running time and ticket prices checked against Heywood Civic’s listing on 28 October 2026.

articles.title: New industrial units planned at Caldershaw Business Centre in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Nine new industrial units are set to be built at Caldershaw Business Centre, aiming to boost local employment and support entrepreneurs.
articles.content_html:
Nine new industrial units are planned for construction at the Caldershaw Business Centre in Rochdale. The initiative aims to create jobs and provide opportunities for local entrepreneurs, according to a proposal submitted to Rochdale Council by Adil Iqbal of IQ7 Ltd.

The new units will occupy a previously disused area of land adjacent to Unit 6/5d at the business centre, which is located off Rooley Moor Road. The site, currently overgrown and littered, previously housed a mill building that has since been demolished.

The development is expected to transform this neglected space into a productive environment for new businesses.

Each of the nine units will range in size from 84 square metres to 164 square metres, featuring roller shutter doors, pedestrian access, small office spaces, and WC facilities.

The total industrial floor space will be approximately 1,170 square metres, providing a significant boost to local business infrastructure and potentially attracting new enterprises to the area.

The planning application is currently under review, with further updates anticipated as the project progresses. This development is significant as it aims to stimulate local entrepreneurship and job creation in Rochdale, addressing the need for more business space in the community.

articles.excerpt: The Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre at Kingsway Business Park has completed its base build, marking a significant step in the development of Rochdale's advanced materials hub.
articles.content_html:
The Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale has reached a major milestone with the completion of its base build.

This development is part of the Atom Valley Innovation District, which aims to foster advanced materials and manufacturing innovation in the region.

Designed by Bond Bryan, the 30,000 sq. ft centre will serve as a vital link between research, specialist facilities, and commercial production.

It is expected to generate £107 million in economic value over the next decade, supporting the transition of new technologies from concept to commercial application.

The Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) has spearheaded the project in collaboration with the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester, and other innovation partners. The next phase will focus on the fit-out of the centre, with operations anticipated to commence in 2027.

Mark Adey, director at Bond Bryan, highlighted the importance of creating environments that facilitate innovation and commercialisation. The SMMC is designed to adapt to emerging technologies and business needs, ensuring it remains relevant as industries evolve.

articles.title: Rochdale council deputy leader detained briefly in Pakistan during civic visit
articles.excerpt: Councillor Daalat Ali was held for a short time upon arrival in Pakistan as part of a delegation aimed at strengthening ties with Sahiwal.
articles.content_html:
Councillor Daalat Ali, the deputy leader of Rochdale council, was detained by authorities for a short period upon his arrival in Pakistan. This incident occurred during a civic delegation visit to the city of Sahiwal, which is twinned with Rochdale.

The delegation includes Rochdale's ceremonial mayor, Councillor Faisal Rana, and aims to strengthen relationships between the two areas, which have historical ties dating back to their twinning in 1998.

The council confirmed that the detention was brief and related to Councillor Ali's long-standing personal campaigning regarding the Kashmir region. A spokesperson for the council stated that such detentions are not uncommon for individuals travelling to this region, particularly those with political views.

Councillor Ali is reported to be safe and well, having continued his travels and meetings with local officials after the incident.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office also acknowledged the situation, confirming that they were in contact with local authorities regarding the matter.

While the exact reasons for Councillor Ali's detention have not been officially confirmed by Pakistani authorities, the council's statement reassured that he was able to resume his duties as part of the delegation shortly thereafter.

This visit is significant for Rochdale, as many residents have familial connections to Sahiwal.

The delegation's activities include attending various events, such as the opening of a Sewing Machine Centre by the Al-Mahmood Foundation, which is part of the ongoing efforts to foster community ties and support local initiatives in both regions.

articles.title: Rochdale’s Deckers Hospitality Group acquires historic drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale-based family group has bought the Malton drinks wholesaler, with existing staff staying and Harry Tate-Smith continuing as trading director.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale-based Deckers Hospitality Group has acquired North Yorkshire drinks wholesaler Tate-Smith, adding a business founded in 1888 to its portfolio.

The deal brings together two family businesses. Deckers is led by siblings Max Brierley and Victoria Cosgrove and operates in hospitality, wholesale and e-commerce.

Tate-Smith, based in Malton, supplies soft and alcoholic drinks across North Yorkshire. The business had been owned by the same family for six generations.

According to the announcement issued on 22 October, it will continue trading as Tate-Smith Ltd. All current staff will remain, and Harry Tate-Smith will continue in the business as trading director.

Paul and Cate Tate-Smith sold the company. Paul said the time was right to pass it to a business that could support its next stage, while retaining a role for their son.

Maxwell Brierley, of Deckers Hospitality Group, said: “Like us Tate-Smith is a family-run business with an impressive history. We felt it was the perfect fit for us as we continue to develop and grow our portfolio, and we welcome them to our family.”

For Rochdale, the acquisition marks an expansion of a locally based group into an established Yorkshire wholesale business. The release does not disclose a purchase price or announce any additional Rochdale jobs.

AAB and Schofield Sweeney advised Tate-Smith’s shareholders. Deckers was advised by Pannone Corporate and Cowgills, part of the Sumer Group.

articles.title: Heywood lollipop man forced to leap out of way as drivers ignore crossing
articles.excerpt: A car and a moped have been seized after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to jump aside for safety.
articles.content_html:
A car and a moped have been seized by Greater Manchester Police after their drivers ignored a lollipop man in Heywood, forcing him to leap out of the way on two separate occasions. The incidents occurred on Bury Old Road on 13 and 14 October, as reported by Rochdale Borough Council.

Barry Jones, the lollipop man involved, was standing in the road when both vehicles failed to stop. The council noted that there have been 137 reported incidents of drivers not stopping for school crossing patrols across the borough in the last five years, highlighting a concerning trend regarding road safety near schools.

Following the incidents, police gathered evidence, including witness statements, which led to the seizure of the silver Skoda car and the moped.

A recent change in law, effective from June, allows police to seize vehicles without issuing a warning first under the Police Reform Act 2002.

Dylan Williams, the cabinet member for highways, expressed gratitude to the police for their prompt action and stated that the council would continue to report such incidents and pursue prosecutions where possible.

This situation underscores the importance of road safety, particularly in school zones, and the need for drivers to adhere to traffic regulations.

articles.title: Police arrest 17 in operation against crime gang in Rochdale and Heywood
articles.excerpt: Seventeen arrests were made during a police operation targeting an organised crime group linked to violence in Heywood earlier this year.
articles.content_html:
Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle an organised crime group in Rochdale and Heywood. This operation, named Operation Rivercrest, involved 250 officers executing a series of raids across multiple locations, including Rochdale, Heywood, Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside, and Yorkshire.

The arrests, which took place on the morning of October 27, 2026, included sixteen men aged between 19 and 49, who are suspected of various offences such as drug supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery.

A 21-year-old woman was also arrested on suspicion of being involved in drug supply.

Detective Sergeant Hannah Taala from Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division stated that the operation was initiated following a violent incident in Heywood earlier this year, which resulted in serious injuries and the use of weapons, including machetes.

A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids, further highlighting the extent of the criminal activities.

The police's focus on this crime group aims to disrupt their operations and enhance community safety. The investigation is ongoing, and further updates are expected as the police continue to address the issues surrounding organised crime in the area.

Motorists and local residents should plan their journeys accordingly, as diversions may be necessary during the roadworks. The council has provided a map of the roadworks and restrictions on their website for those seeking further details.

This development is significant for local commuters and residents, as it may affect access to nearby businesses and homes. For the latest updates and to view the roadworks map, visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

The next steps will involve the commencement of construction works, with further updates expected as the project progresses. This development is significant for local families, particularly those with children who have SEND, as it will provide them with improved recreational opportunities in their community.

articles.title: Does a boggart still haunt Clegg Hall?
articles.excerpt: The stone house by the Rochdale Canal is real, its 19th‑century boggart story is real — but the murders that feed the tale are not supported by contemporary records.
articles.summary: The stone house by the Rochdale Canal is real, its 19th‑century boggart story is real — but the murders that feed the tale are not supported by contemporary records.
articles.body:
Clegg Hall is a genuine early‑17th‑century house standing where Clegg Hall Road climbs from Smithy Bridge toward Littleborough; it is protected as a Grade II* listed building (List Entry Number 1309615). ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

The building’s stones and beams are historical fact; the boggart is a thing of story. The best short answer for a reader asking whether the boggart still haunts the place is therefore practical: the hall survives, the local tradition survives with it, but the grisly murders at the heart of the legend are recorded only in folklore, not in surviving contemporary records. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

Where the story comes from

The tale that made Clegg Hall notorious in print was collected and published by 19th‑century folklorists. John Roby printed a graphic version of “Clegg‑Hall Boggart” in his Traditions of Lancashire, drawing on local ballads and informants; variants include a ballad transmitted by William Nuttall in which a relative called “Sir Roland” murders children to seize the estate. Those published accounts are the primary sources for the plot people now recall. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

What the county history says

County and parish historians who examined the story in the 19th century treated it as folklore rather than documentary fact. The chapter on old houses and families in the History of the Parish of Rochdale records the same tradition — heirs despatched to secure the hall — but explicitly warns that Roby’s narrative is “pure imagination” when set against surviving legal, visitation and parish records. The historian notes that the tale was widespread enough to produce a local proverb, “as ill as Clegg Hall boggart,” which shows how the story entered local speech. ([your-content.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com](https://your-content.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/04145039/chapter-xvii-old-houses-and-old-families-butterworth-pages337-389.pdf))

What is documented

Architectural and estate records place Clegg Hall as a medieval site later rebuilt in stone around the early 1600s; deeds and visitation material record the Clegg, Belfield and later families in the neighbourhood. The National Heritage List entry gives the hall its legal protection and summarises its architectural significance; that is the best source for verifiable facts about the building itself. There is no surviving contemporary court, parish or chancery record that corroborates the specific murders described in the boggart tales. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

How folklore and local speech changed the story

As with many rural English legends, Roby and later collectors assembled versions that vary in key details: method of killing (moat or dagger), identity of the murderer, whether the victims were children or tenants, and the precise era — some tellings push the origin back into the medieval period, others leave it vague. Those variations, and the lack of a single contemporaneous source, are typical signs that the account is oral tradition evolving through retelling rather than an eyewitness or legal record. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25256/25256-h/25256-h.htm))

So, does the boggart still haunt Clegg Hall?

If “haunting” means a persistent local story and a place in the region’s folklore, then yes: the boggart remains part of Rochdale’s storytelling landscape. If “haunting” means a verifiable crime, a named accused or a historic legal finding that proves the murders happened as described, the answer is no — those elements are not found in the archive material historians have identified. Readers who want to follow the paper trail should start with the National Heritage List entry for the building and the 19th‑century printed collections (Roby and the parish histories) that preserved the tale. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

What a curious local can do

If you want to see the hall from public paths, Clegg Hall sits near the Rochdale Canal at Smithy Bridge; the Historic England entry gives the statutory description of the building. For anyone wishing to check the archives themselves, the county and parish histories cited above point to deeds and visitation records — the original evidence historians relied on when separating estate fact from later fiction. If new documentary evidence surfaced, historians would treat it on its merits; until then the boggart is best read as durable folklore lodged around a very real house. ([historicengland.org.uk](https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1309615))

articles.title: Two Rochdale men among ten charged in drugs supply investigation
articles.excerpt: GMP says two Rochdale men are among ten people charged following a seven-month investigation. All ten have been remanded ahead of a Crown Court appearance.
articles.content_html:
Two Rochdale men are among ten people charged following a seven-month investigation into the suspected supply and distribution of drugs across Greater Manchester and the West Midlands.

Greater Manchester Police named the local defendants as Jailil Ahmed, 53, of Twinegate, Rochdale, and Shakil Ahmed, 51, of Whittaker Lane, Rochdale.

In a statement issued on 27 October, the force said eight men, a woman and a 16-year-old boy had been charged with conspiracy to supply controlled drugs in classes A, B and C, and conspiracy to supply an unauthorised medicinal product.

The boy cannot be named for legal reasons. The other adult defendants are from Burnage and Wolverhampton, or have no fixed abode, according to the police statement.

GMP said its Serious and Organised Crime Group carried out the investigation into suspected large-scale supply and distribution in the two regions.

All ten have been remanded in custody ahead of a scheduled appearance at Manchester Crown Court on Friday 13 November 2026, the force said.

The charges are allegations. No finding of guilt should be inferred, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless and until convicted.

articles.content_html:
Middleton is making final preparations for its Christmas lights switch-on event, scheduled for Saturday, November 14, in Middleton Gardens. The festive atmosphere is already taking shape with decorations appearing throughout the town, including a special red shoe outside Middleton Library in memory of Rochdale Council officer Lauren Mason, who passed away two years ago.

The switch-on event will begin at 12pm and will feature a variety of attractions designed to engage the community and spread festive cheer.

Attendees can look forward to food and drink stalls, fairground rides, and market stalls, including the Teenage Market, which supports local young entrepreneurs. The Art House will host personalised Christmas card-making sessions and face painting for children.

As the day progresses, visitors will enjoy performances from local community groups, culminating in a performance by Middleton Brass Band at 4.30pm, which will help set the festive mood ahead of the lights being switched on.

This event not only marks the start of the Christmas season in Middleton but also provides an opportunity for local businesses and young entrepreneurs to showcase their offerings.

Residents and visitors alike are encouraged to attend and participate in the festivities, making it a significant occasion for the community.

articles.title: Broad Lane roadworks in Rochdale set to begin on 11 January 2027
articles.excerpt: Roadworks on Broad Lane will temporarily close part of the road from January to May 2027, affecting local traffic.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on Broad Lane will commence on 11 January 2027 and are expected to last until 2 May 2027. The works will involve the temporary closure of Broad Lane from the junction with Oldham Road to the junction with Turf Hill Road.

During this period, traffic will be diverted to alternative routes including Oldham Road, Queensway, Kingsway, and Turf Hill Road. Local residents and commuters are advised to plan their journeys accordingly to avoid delays.

The roadworks are part of ongoing improvements aimed at enhancing local infrastructure and ensuring safer travel for all road users. The council has provided a map of the affected area and alternative routes on its website.

Residents are encouraged to check the Rochdale Borough Council's official website for updates on the progress of the roadworks. This development is significant for local traffic management and will impact daily commutes in the area.
